summary: Printable copy of a blue spare foot for an upright perforated game board. In use the foot stands on the end faces of its two U arms, the half ring vertical, and the narrow 12.8 end of the board's side rail clips into the U-channel handle on top. The channel is a clip: lips at the opening (outer side) narrow it to 12.9 (original 12.7) and grip the 12.8 rail end; below them it widens to 15.2 (original 15.0). PLA, printed lying on its floor (open side up), no supports.

assumptions: A1: the arcs are concentric half circles centred on the arm-end plane: inner radius D4 checks against the photo within 0.7 mm.
A2: the 4 round marks and 2 small dots in the floor are moulding ejector marks and are not copied.

A3: the channel is a clip. Lips at the opening (outer side) grip the board rail's 12.8 end; below them it widens to the original's 15.0 (user: 'it is outer side to catch ... clip on'; board photos 215353, 215421, 215633). The 3.3 reading (214111) is not used.
A4: rim top is flat; no lips, fillets or draft on the ring walls (none visible in the photos).
A5: bed 250 x 210 (Prusa MK4 class); every Bambu bed is larger.

A6: lips use PLA press (0.05 per side), the wide part PLA snug (0.10 per side). PLA is stiffer than the original's soft plastic: if the clip is too hard to push on or cracks, open the lips in 0.05 steps (processed/fits-PLA.json press) or print in PETG.
A7: quantity 1 (one replacement foot); the board uses one at each side.
A8: ring sizes D1, D5, D17 and the wall thicknesses only set the footprint and look; photo estimates are acceptable for them.
A9: in use the arm-end faces (Y = 0) are the feet: both lie flat in one plane, and the print copies that exactly.
